messages:
kevin: heads-up: hit a puzzler in the python sdk sample where async tool calls return a wrapped JSON string and our dataclass coercer chokes. also saw duplicate tool side-effects when auth refresh raced with retry.

kevin: repro snippet (very small):

kevin: ```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key="...")

@dataclass
class Score:
    id: str
    value: float

# tool actually returns '"{\"id\": \"x\", \"value\": 0.9}\"' (stringified json)
res = await client.tool_call(
    "get_score",
    input={"id": "x"},
    output_type=Score,
)
print(res)
```

kevin: when token refresh happens the transport retries and the tool receives the request twice (duplicate counter increment). logs show: request_id=zz1 send -> refresh -> retry -> tool invoked x2.

laura: the two problems are related: coercion + idempotency. if we send an idempotency key by default for non-read-only tool calls the server can dedupe. meanwhile coercion should try to json.loads the raw string before dataclass coercion.

mike: +1. also streaming is an add'l angle: some tools stream NDJSON, some stream partial json chunks. SDK currently treats each chunk as a complete object which fails for split frames.

mike: proposal: new opt-ins on AsyncClient.tool_call / stream_tool_call: 
- idempotency_key: optional str (auto-generate if None and user opts-in)
- coerce_mode: one of ["off","lenient","strict"] where lenient tries json.loads when value is a string
- assemble_stream: bool for stream_tool_call to buffer partial frames until a full json object parses

julie: for typing parity: output_type should accept typing.Union and typing.Annotated with metadata like origin. e.g. Union[Ok, Err] -> we return a TaggedUnion with variant and parsed value. docs need to show how to inspect which variant matched.

kevin: ergonomics ask: surface sdk-generated request_id and idempotency_key on the response object so apps can log them (right now only in debug logs).

laura: security: sending idempotency headers is fine, but server-side TTL and auth scope must be used to avoid cross-tenant dedupe. server should only dedupe within customer context.

mike: implementation notes:
- transport: if refresh in-flight, block retry until refresh completes for that request instead of blindly retrying. simple lock per-connection/request will do.
- coercion: try sequence: if output_type provided then
    1) if raw is string -> try json.loads(raw)
    2) if json.loads returns basic types -> map into dataclass/typing logic
    3) if fails and on_parse_failure hook provided, call it with raw+exc
- streaming: keep a small buffer and attempt json.loads when buffer contains closing brace or newline; expose max_buffer_bytes.

julie: tests to add: stringified-json -> dataclass, union resolution ordering, stream multi-frame assembly, token-refresh race causing single vs double invocation. add sample-app tests and a small ndjson server in examples repo.

kevin: created a tiny repro repo: https://github.com/redwood/repro-examples/tree/kevin/toolcall-coerce-idempotency with a README and failing tests.

ops-bot: created issue redwood/sdk#3678 "python sdk: tool_call coercion + idempotency + stream assembly" assigned to @mike. https://github.com/redwood/sdk/issues/3678

laura: i'll draft an API PR that adds the coerce_mode param + response.request_id + response.idempotency_key. mike can take the transport/token-lock part. julie can own stream assembly.

mike: sounds good. i'll add unit tests that monkeypatch the transport and assert only one downstream invocation when refresh triggers. also add a small integration test for stringified-json coercion.

kevin: thanks all — customer affected by this will be happy to see a hotfix. ping me for review. :thumbsup:
